## 5. One Non-Obvious Thing I Noticed

**The Construct is a 50-commit day where one agent did all the work — and that agent can't trade.**

WOLF executed 50 commits today, making it by far the most active author in the repo's history. Yet every one of those commits was a status update on a halted, non-compliant portfolio. WOLF is fully operational (polling, signaling, committing) but structurally frozen on equity execution. Meanwhile, all other Construct agents — the 19 others listed in the manifest — produced zero output. The multi-agent architecture that's supposed to provide cross-checks (Sentinel for risk, Keystone for regime, Atlas for intelligence) is silent precisely when WOLF most needs outside signal.

The non-obvious pattern: **the system's activity metric (commits) and its capability metric (actionable decisions) are completely decoupled today.** High commit velocity can mask zero forward progress. The standup numbers look busy; the trading book is stuck. Tomorrow's forcing function is the rebalance — but no agent other than WOLF has a stake in whether it fires correctly.
